A support check uses pass/fail/unknown. A known negative supporting observation can inform a requested check; it is not automatically uncertainty. Use unknown when the evidence cannot establish the requested fact. Do not count supporting facts as completed edits. Assess only the supplied check, not the overall instruction label.

n1: The node’s target and relation are basically well bound: the source clearly contains one blue book and one rose, and the edit does not place the book behind the rose. The main issue is the partial criterion: “the book has been moved” can count unrelated displacement toward the flower as progress even when the required depth relation is absent. Make partial depend on observable, source-to-edit progress specifically toward the book/flower behind-ordering, not mere proximity or movement; reserve absent for no such progress and unknown for insufficient evidence. Compare the same identified objects across source and edit, and avoid treating extra flowers or book alteration as progress. The traces conflict on whether there was movement, so require evidence for that distinction rather than inferring it from proximity; retain the complete criterion and do not force a label. All traces are valid, queried, and dependency-free, so this is not a transport or schema failure. The aggregate’s 0.8 agreement is already high; use the disagreement to sharpen the partial/absent boundary, not to change the requested relation or optimize toward the reference label alone.
